pr.title: Add a skill that walks reviewers through a large pull request
pr.head: 5f6878126e84415296560b045e6ff7d5ed41b4b8

summary: Adds walkthrough-pr, a skill that turns a large pull request into one page: the diff split into logical groups in reading order, each opened by what it does, what to hold in mind and a checklist, then every hunk syntax-highlighted with viewed and reviewed state.

The page framework is a fixed renderer, walkthrough.js and walkthrough.css, so the agent only writes a JSON spec with the grouping, the explanations and the checks. walkthrough.py, standard library plus gh, validates the spec against the diff and writes the page. This page is itself a walkthrough of the pull request, built by the stacked Pages work.

groups.title: The skill and its spec format
groups.kicker: What the agent reads: when to use the skill, how to group, and the JSON it writes
intro: SKILL.md is the workflow: resolve the PR, init a spec, read the diff and its context, fill the spec, build, publish, and update when the PR moves. Most of it is guidance on judgment: order groups from the contract outward, put every file in exactly one group, explain why, and write checks a reviewer can act on.
spec.md documents the JSON. Every text field is inserted as HTML, so notes can use <code> and tables with the listed classes.

checks.text: Reading a PR never authorizes changing it: the skill says not to comment, push or approve unless asked.
Publishing is host-neutral: a local file always works, Claude Artifacts is an enhancement, as the repository's portability rules require.
The skill says to keep the spec in the host's scratch directory. That keeps it private but loses it when the session ends; the stacked PR's Pages branch is where specs become durable.

files.note: The workflow and the grouping guidance.
The spec schema and the HTML classes cards may use.

groups.title: The build script
groups.kicker: walkthrough.py: parse the diff, validate the spec against it, embed both in a page
intro: parse_diff turns unified diff text into files with hunks and per-line old and new numbers, and classifies each file's language and kind (generated, test, docs). The anchor is GitHub's own files-tab anchor, the SHA-256 of the path, so each file links straight to its place in the PR.

validate collects every problem before failing: a file in no group, in two groups, a path outside the diff, a duplicate group id, a malformed check. page embeds the data as JSON in a script tag, escaping </ so a diff line cannot close it.

checks.text: The moved-head guard in build compares the spec's head to the live PR, so a page never shows a diff other than the one its notes describe.
Standard library only, plus the gh CLI; no dependency is added to the Python package.

gh pr diff fails for very large PRs; the skill documents a git diff fallback through --diff. The stacked PR moves the default to the compare API by merge base and head, which also makes older heads rebuildable.

groups.title: The renderer
groups.kicker: Fixed JS and CSS that build the whole page from the embedded data
intro: walkthrough.js renders the sidebar, overview, groups and files from the JSON, then wires the interactions: collapse and expand, viewed and reviewed state in localStorage keyed by repo and PR, copy-path buttons, sticky file headers that square their corners while pinned, and highlight.js per hunk side so multi-line tokens survive.
walkthrough.css carries the light and dark palettes as tokens and the diff tints; syntax colours come from the same tokens.

checks.text: Remote scripts come only from cdnjs and fonts only from Google Fonts, which keeps the page valid as a Claude Artifact; a test pins it.
Files that start collapsed are highlighted when first opened, so a large PR still loads quickly.

groups.title: Tests and packaging
groups.kicker: Parsing, validation, output, and the published skill set
intro: test_walkthrough.py covers line numbering, kinds, GitHub anchors, the page and renderer output, each spec refusal and the CDN allowlist, all against an inline fixture diff. test_packaging.py adds the skill to the exact published set both plugin manifests must ship.

checks.text: The fixture diff includes a </script> string, and the test asserts it cannot end the data block.

groups.title: Plan and README
groups.kicker: Why the skill exists and where it goes next
intro: The new plan, docs/projects/pr-walkthrough, states the outcome, the acceptance criteria, and the hosting decision: Artifacts now, GitHub Pages per repository next, no external site. The README lists the new skill.
